editorial.headline: Metal Fasteners With a Clean National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25952 covers the manufacture of nails, nuts, bolts, rivets, tacks, and similar threaded metal goods, open nationally and not blocked for Bali PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25952 is a manufacturing classification for the small metal pieces that hold larger systems together: nails, nuts, bolts, and similar threaded goods made from iron, steel, copper, aluminium, and other metals. Its scope also reaches plug nails or rivets and thumbtacks. In plain English, this is not a trading code and not a broad machinery category; it is the industrial making of metal fastening components themselves.

The record opens this activity across the full scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not reserved in the slim record for only one business size. A founder reading it should understand the category as available from smaller production setups through larger industrial operations, while still staying within the activity described: manufacturing the named metal fasteners and closely similar threaded goods.

The national PMA picture is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower cap in the slim record, so the editorial answer should be direct: nationally, this activity is open to foreign investment up to the stated ceiling. No extra capital rule, permit sequence, licence name, or operational threshold is added here because the slim record does not provide one.

Bali does not change that into a prohibition on the facts provided. The Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says it is not blocked. The reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That sits against the moratorium rule in the record, which blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali province. For this code, the honest national-vs-Bali picture is therefore clean: foreign ownership is nationally open up to 100%, and Bali is not marked as blocked for PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.
